messages:
zara_rm: Heads-up — canary (model-serving v2.6.0) at 30% in us-west is tripping p95 latency alarms. deploy-bot flagged a 28% spike vs baseline around 17:12 UTC. Should we let auto-rollback run or take a manual, staged approach?
kevin_sre: saw it too. errors are low, tail latency only. auto-rollback is enabled but threshold close to borderline. leaning staged revert + pin first.
anita_eng: +1 to staged. if we full revert immediately we risk masking root cause, and dedicated customers on reserved pools might be impacted.
deploy-bot: Alert: canary:us-west:v2.6.0 | p95=980ms (+28%) | auto-rollback=armed at 1000ms for 10m. To cancel: `deploy-bot cancel-auto-rollback 1717804321`
zara_rm: okay — plan suggestion: 1) cancel auto-rollback (so we control pacing), 2) pin default route back to v2.5.3 for new sessions in us-west (gradual traffic cut), 3) monitor 15m, then either rollforward with fix or full revert. comms: short note to customers on impacted region + release notes update.
kevin_sre: commands: ```
# cancel automated rollback
releasetool autopilot cancel --id 1717804321
# pin route for new sessions
releasetool route pin --service inference-api --region us-west --to v2.5.3 --sessions new --reason "latency spike canary"
# increase telemetry retention for this window
opsctl metrics retention set --service inference-api --window 60m
```
sam_platform: I'll run the pin in 2 min and keep traffic at 20% initial cut (so v2.6 stays at 10% for warm sessions). @kevin_sre can you confirm the canary dashboard link?
kevin_sre: dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.io/d/serving/canary?orgId=1&var-region=us-west&var-version=v2.6.0 — watching p95, cpu, kv-cache-misses.
maya_cs: I'll draft the blurb for customers: "We're observing increased request latency in US-West for the latest inference rollout; routing for new sessions will be temporarily pinned to previous version while we investigate. No action required on your side." Want to send after pin goes live?
anita_eng: also add a note in release notes: under v2.6.0 -> "Investigating p95 regression in US-West; temporary staged rollback applied for new sessions."
zara_rm: agreed. executing now: @sam_platform please run the commands and post status. I'll notify execs and CS once pinned.
sam_platform: running: `releasetool autopilot cancel --id 1717804321` -> OK
`releasetool route pin --service inference-api --region us-west --to v2.5.3 --sessions new --traffic-cut 20%` -> OK
realtime: p95 down from 980ms -> 720ms in 6m. continuing to monitor.
kevin_sre: good signal improvement. cpu still normal, kv-cache-misses reduced. keep retention up. set alert to notify if p95 > 900ms for 5m.
deploy-bot: Action logged: manual-pin applied by sam_platform for 1717804321; autopilot canceled.
maya_cs: sending customer note now to impacted accounts and posting in #customer-notify draft channel.
zara_rm: follow-up decision: if p95 stays <=800ms for 15m we keep staged pin and rollforward with a small config tweak later today. if it rebounds above 900ms for >5m, we full revert traffic to v2.5.3 and open incident. Agreed?
anita_eng: agreed. I'll prepare a hotfix branch for v2.6 and start bisecting changes that affect attention kernel scheduling.
sam_platform: holding for 20m window. will update thread with final state.
(some time later)
sam_platform: 20m check-in: p95 stable ~710ms. keeping staged pin. not doing a full revert. closing the immediate rollback plan. I'll update release notes and mark the rollback flag as resolved.
zara_rm: Thanks team. Recording postmortem action items: 1) tighten canary thresholds for model-serving tail latency, 2) add KV-cache-miss metric to auto-rollback policy, 3) run isolated perf test for v2.6 build. I'll open a ticket. :white_check_mark:
kevin_sre: noted. tagging oncall for next 24h vigilance.
end of thread
